Next pass, in this order:
1. THE BACK CLIFF. The south side is a flat sheer grey wall, the biggest blank area on the build. Make it a real crag: rock buttresses and gullies, strata ledges, overhangs, a few clinging pines, and a zig-zag service path with a small postern door into the lower court.
2. THE THRONE HALL APSE. Build it as a real semicircular apse projecting outward from the Palas wall, with its own conical slate roof and gold finial, tall round-arched windows around its curve, and inside it the raised gold throne platform in the curved end.
3. THE PALAS BACK FACADE. The south elevation still reads as a grid. Give it the same pilaster bays and per-storey Romanesque window groups as the front, and add a projecting oriel tower (a bay window rising three storeys on corbels, with its own small cap).
4. THE FRONT APPROACH. From the street view the stair-turret spire is barely visible behind the gatehouse. Make it read from the front: thin the gatehouse roofline in front of it if needed, and add a winding approach road up the crag to the gate with a low parapet wall and lanterns.
5. COURTYARD LIFE. A fountain in the upper courtyard, lanterns, banners, a cart, flower boxes.
Keep everything else as it is.
summary: All five points are done in the generator (new parts backcliff, road, apse, courtyard) and build.nbt is re-saved. check shows 0 floating blocks and 0 unsupported attachments; the 56 orphans are small leftovers. I rendered it and looked at the south and corner views; the apse and oriel are small in them, and I did not take close-ups.
applied: 1 Back cliff: rebuilt the south crag with per-x buttresses and gullies, strata ledges with undercuts, and mossy ledge tops. Added clinging spruces, a two-switchback zig-zag service path, and a small postern door in a short wall on the upper court's south edge.

2 Apse: added a semicircular apse on the Palas south wall (x93..101, projecting about 4) on a rock buttress. It has five tall round-arched windows, a conical slate roof with a gold finial, and inside a raised gold platform with a gold and blue throne in the curved end.

3 Back facade: added a three-storey oriel (x75..79) on stepped corbels with its own small slate cap. Added quartz-and-sandstone string courses between the storeys. The existing pilaster bays and per-storey window groups on the south side were kept.

4 Front approach: added a winding stair-ramp road that snakes up the west crag front to the causeway foot, with a low stone-brick parapet and lantern posts. Shortened the east gate tower and its cap, which stood directly in front of the stair-turret spire, and shortened the roof flagpole.

5 Courtyard life: added a fountain (basin, water, pillar, upper bowl, lantern) in the upper court. Added lamp posts, two banner poles, a cart with hay and a barrel, and flower boxes plus lozenge banners on the Knights' House east wall.
skipped: The postern leads into the upper court, not the lower court. The lower court is at the front, behind the Palas, so it is not reachable from the south cliff.
The back cliff is only about 4 to 5 blocks deep because the grid is 52 deep, so the buttresses, gullies and ledges are shallow relief.

The winding road is one west-side leg that snakes in z, not a multi-leg switchback, because the front crag is only about 5 blocks deep. The oriel and apse sit close to existing pilasters and windows (the apse swallows the pilaster at x=99).
I did not render close-ups of the apse, oriel and road at full zoom.
